Breakfast at the hotel.

Head to Xochimilco for a boat ride along its famous canals. The Aztecs used these waterways to travel across the Basin of Mexico. The canals survive as evidence of a culture that flourished here more than 500 years ago. UNESCO recognised their cultural and geographical significance when Xochimilco was listed as a World Heritage Site in 1987.

Continue to Coyoacán for a food walk through markets, street stalls, family-run restaurants and modern eateries. Along the way, your guide will share stories and local anecdotes about the neighbourhood. Get to know Coyoacán through its streets, its people and the food they make every day.

Mexico City – Teotihuacán – Tacos and Mezcal Tour

Breakfast at the hotel.

The archaeological ruins of Teotihuacán lie about 50 km northeast of Mexico City. The massive Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon rise above the complex. Mountains surround and shelter the ancient city, which was probably founded in the early first century CE and reached its peak around the year 500. At the time, its influence extended as far as Guatemala to the south and present-day Texas to the north.

Walk along the Avenue of the Dead with a local guide, see the main structures and imagine what life here was like nearly 2,000 years ago.

Back in Mexico City, the day turns to food. Visit traditional taquerías and try different takes on Mexico’s best-known dish. See how widely taco styles vary across the city and discover which flavours are local favourites after dark. The tasting also introduces you to mezcal.
